correctness.rationale: For p<q, phi(pq)=(p-1)(q-1), so gcd(pq,phi(pq))>1 is equivalent exactly to p|(q-1). For fixed p, PNT in reduced residue class 1 mod p gives pi(x/p;p,1)~x/[p(p-1)log x]. With z fixed, the range z<p<=x^(1/3) is O(x/log x * sum_(p>z)1/[p(p-1)]) by Brun--Titchmarsh and log(x/p^2)>=log(x)/3. For x^(1/3)<p<sqrt x, writing q=kp+1, k<=x/p^2 gives O(x^(2/3)). Let z increase to infinity to obtain E(x)~A x/log x. Divide by Landau squarefree-semiprime count ~x loglog x/log x. The exact local condition and finite computations do not alone prove the asymptotic.
residual_risks: Relies on standard prime-number theorem in arithmetic progressions, Brun--Titchmarsh, and Landau semiprime estimate; no effective error term claimed.

value.rationale: An explicit sharp first-order law for noncyclic group orders within squarefree semiprimes contrasts with their near-universality in this stratum and with scarcity of cyclic group orders globally. The convergent prime constant supplies a quantitative baseline for higher fixed-prime-factor strata, where obstructions interact; more than a restatement of the elementary pq criterion.
residual_risks: Mathematical significance is restricted to the first nontrivial multiplicative layer, not a global new counting theorem.

limitations: Asymptotic restricted to squarefree semiprimes; prime powers and >=3 distinct prime factors excluded.
